sentences.text:
Coram : Hon'ble Mr. Justice B.S. Walia
Present : Mr. Sandeep Kotla, Advocate for the appellant.

Ms. Rahish Pahwa, Advocate for respondent No.1.
 ***
B.S. Walia, J. (Oral)

[1] Challenge in the instant appeal is to award dated 08.09.2004 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Faridabad awarding compensation of Rs.1,11,000/- to respondent No. 1 along with interest on account of injuries received in the motor vehicular accident resulting in his suffering 15% permanent disability in a motor vehicular accident on 18.04.2002 on the bus of the appellant hitting the car of the respondent No.1-claimant.
[2] Learned Counsel for the appellant contends that the impugned award is legally unsustainable as there is no evidence of negligence which is a sine qua non for awarding compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 nor was any FIR registered against the driver of the offending vehicle and it was the Maruti 800 car of respondent No. 1 which struck against the axle of the bus as a result of which the axle of the bus broke and its rear wheels got detached and the bus turned turtle.

sentences.text: [3] Learned Counsel for respondent No. 1-claimant on the other hand 1 of 2 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:049067 FAO-33-2005 (2) 2023:PHHC:049067 contends that it needs no mention that even if the axle of the bus had broken as a result of which it became uncontrollable, the accident would not have taken place had the bus not been driven at a high speed.
Even otherwise, it is unbelievable that a Maruti 800 car can strike against the axle/rear wheels of the bus unless and until the Maruti car goes under the bus in question.

Learned Counsel for the appellant however fairly concedes that it is not the stand of the appellant that the Maruti 800 car went under the bus and as a result thereof, hit the axle of the bus as a result of which the rear wheels of the bus got detached.

Learned Counsel concedes that axle of the bus was already broken and was hanging outside the bus and that in the circumstances, the bus could not be controlled while on the road as a result of which the accident took place with the uncontrollablebus hitting the Maruti 800 car.

[4] The position as noted above, makes it clear that the axle of the bus had broken and due to it being at high speed the bus was uncontrollable as a result of which it hit against the Maruti Car and also overturned resulting in injuries to respondent No.1-claimant.

[5] In the circumstances, I find no infirmity in the award passed by the learned MACT, Faridabad especially in view of the fact that the driver of the offending bus owned by the appellant did not put in appearance before the Tribunal.
Compensation as deposited before the MACT, Faridabad be released to the respondent- claimant.
